prompt:
The speed v of a transverse wave on a stretched wire is believed to depend on the tension F (a force) and the linear mass density mu (mass per unit length) according to the relationship:
v = C * F^p * mu^q
where C is a dimensionless constant, and p and q are unknown numerical indices.
(a) State the SI base units of v, F, and mu. [1]
(b) By equating powers of base units on both sides of the equation, determine the values of the indices p and q. [2]

mark_scheme.criterion: State [v] = m s^-1, [F] = kg m s^-2, [mu] = kg m^-1.
Set up index equations: kg^(p+q) m^(p-q) s^(-2p) = kg^0 m^1 s^-1, leading to -2p = -1 and p + q = 0.
Solve to obtain p = 1/2 and q = -1/2.

hints: Substitute base units into v = F^p * mu^q and collect powers of kg, m, and s.
Compare the power of s on both sides to find p first.
solution: (a) [v] = m s^-1, [F] = kg m s^-2, [mu] = kg m^-1. (b) m s^-1 = kg^(p+q) m^(p-q) s^(-2p). Equating powers: s: -2p = -1 => p = 1/2. kg: p + q = 0 => q = -1/2.
teacher_walkthrough: (a) Base units: speed is m s^-1; tension force is kg m s^-2; linear density is kg m^-1.
(b) Express right side in base units: (kg m s^-2)^p * (kg m^-1)^q = kg^(p+q) * m^(p-q) * s^(-2p).
Equate powers with left side (kg^0 m^1 s^-1):
Check length (m): p - q = 1/2 - (-1/2) = 1. Matches m^1.
Result: p = 1/2, q = -1/2 (giving v = C * sqrt(F / mu)).

provenance.independence_statement: Authored as a 3-mark power derivation for wave speed on a wire.
